questions.sec: Spondyloarthritis classification, shared features and non-radiographic axial SpA
questions.q: Which branch of the printed SpA classification tree lists shoulder and hip as root joints?
opts: Peripheral spondyloarthropathy limited to knee and elbow
questions.exp: The classification tree places shoulder and hip (root joints) under axial SpA, which then divides into non-radiographic and radiographic axial SpA. (Book p532)

questions.sec: Spondyloarthritis classification, shared features and non-radiographic axial SpA
questions.q: Which trio is printed under the peripheral SpA arm of the classification tree?
opts: Reactive arthritis, psoriatic arthritis and IBD (enteropathic) arthritis
questions.exp: Peripheral SpA (peripheral involvement greater than axial) lists reactive arthritis, psoriatic arthritis and IBD enteropathic arthritis. (Book p532)

questions.sec: Spondyloarthritis classification, shared features and non-radiographic axial SpA
questions.q: How does the source equate juvenile idiopathic arthritis within the SpA tree?
opts: JIA is a subset of radiographic axial SpA only
JIA is excluded from the SpA classification
JIA equals non-radiographic axial SpA with no peripheral disease
JIA is also called juvenile onset SpA
questions.exp: The tree annotates juvenile idiopathic arthritis as AKA juvenile onset SpA. (Book p532)

questions.sec: Spondyloarthritis classification, shared features and non-radiographic axial SpA
questions.q: Which HLA association and degree are printed among SpA shared features?
opts: HLA B27 association in varying degrees
HLA B51 as the universal SpA marker
HLA DR4 in 100% of cases only
questions.exp: Shared features begin with HLA B27 association (varying degrees). (Book p532)

questions.sec: Spondyloarthritis classification, shared features and non-radiographic axial SpA
questions.q: What is the printed most common extra-articular manifestation of SpA?
opts: Keratitis as the sole ocular feature
Acute anterior alternating asymmetric uveitis (4A uveitis)
questions.exp: Features list m/c extra-articular manifestation as acute anterior alternating asymmetric uveitis (4A uveitis). (Book p532)

questions.sec: Spondyloarthritis classification, shared features and non-radiographic axial SpA
questions.q: Which statement among the printed SpA features favors SpA over rheumatoid arthritis?
opts: 4A uveitis as the most common extra-articular manifestation
Association with plaque-type psoriasis in the peripheral arm
Absence of rheumatoid factor and of subcutaneous nodules with RA extra-articular features
Significant familial aggregation with HLA B27 association
questions.exp: SpA features print absence of rheumatoid factor and absence of subcutaneous nodules and extra-articular features of RA. (Book p532)

questions.sec: Spondyloarthritis classification, shared features and non-radiographic axial SpA
questions.q: A young patient has inflammatory back pain worse with rest and better with activity, alternating buttock pain, and no plain-film sacroiliitis. Which printed label applies?
questions.exp: Non-radiographic axial SpA clinical features are inflammatory back pain (exacerbated by rest, relieved by activity), alternating buttock pain due to sacroiliitis and deep low back pain, with no radiographic evidence of sacroiliitis. (Book p532)

questions.sec: Spondyloarthritis classification, shared features and non-radiographic axial SpA
questions.q: What imaging and serology notes are printed for non-radiographic axial SpA?
opts: No radiographic sacroiliitis; MRI may show active sacroiliitis; may have HLA B27
Plain x-ray always shows grade 3 sacroiliitis; MRI never informative
HLA B27 is always negative by definition
questions.exp: Non-radiographic axial SpA: no radiographic evidence (x-ray features of sacroiliitis), MRI may show active sacroiliitis and it may have HLA B27 association. (Book p532)

questions.sec: Spondyloarthritis classification, shared features and non-radiographic axial SpA
questions.q: What proportion of non-radiographic axial SpA converts to radiographic axial SpA over 5–10 years, and what does the right arm list?
opts: 90% in 5 years; only osteopenia without syndesmophytes
5% in 5–10 years; x-ray features include syndesmophytes, bony ankylosis, bamboo spine and spinal fracture
10% in 20 years; only disc space narrowing
questions.exp: The conversion arrow prints 5% in 5–10 years to radiographic axial SpA whose x-ray features of sacroiliitis are syndesmophytes, bony ankylosis, bamboo spine and spinal fracture; extra-articular manifestations may be seen. (Book p532)

questions.sec: Radiographic axial SpA pathogenesis, presentation and inflammatory back pain
questions.q: According to the pathogenesis block, inflammatory granulation tissue directly causes which two changes?
opts: Erosion of annulus fibrosis and nucleus pulposus, and calcification of peripheral annular fibres producing syndesmophytes
questions.exp: Inflammatory granulation tissue lists erosion of annulus fibrosis and nucleus pulposus, and calcification of peripheral fibres of annulus fibrosis as syndesmophytes. (Book p533)

questions.sec: Radiographic axial SpA pathogenesis, presentation and inflammatory back pain
questions.q: How does the source characterize the vertical osteophyte that arises from syndesmophyte calcification?
opts: Lateral and non-continuous with the disc
Restricted to the posterior elements only
questions.exp: Under the calcification arm the vertical osteophyte is annotated thin, delicate, marginal, symmetrical. (Book p533)

questions.sec: Radiographic axial SpA pathogenesis, presentation and inflammatory back pain
questions.q: What mechanical sequence is printed after gliding of vertebra over one another?
opts: Bony ankylosis leading to bamboo spine and square-wave vertebra (loss of concavity)
questions.exp: Gliding of vertebra over one another leads to bony ankylosis, producing bamboo spine and square wave vertebra (loss of concavity). (Book p533)

questions.sec: Radiographic axial SpA pathogenesis, presentation and inflammatory back pain
questions.q: Which complication level is printed as most common for spinal fracture in this chapter?
questions.exp: Complication lists spinal fracture with m/c site C5–C6. (Book p533)

questions.sec: Radiographic axial SpA pathogenesis, presentation and inflammatory back pain
questions.q: Which inflammatory mediators are printed for radiographic axial SpA?
questions.exp: Inflammatory mediators listed are TNF alpha and IL-17, IL-23. (Book p533)

questions.sec: Radiographic axial SpA pathogenesis, presentation and inflammatory back pain
questions.q: What dual presentation framework organizes the clinical features of radiographic axial SpA?
questions.exp: Presentation is structured as synovitis plus enthesitis (inflammation of tendon, ligament, capsule, fascia). (Book p533)

questions.sec: Radiographic axial SpA pathogenesis, presentation and inflammatory back pain
questions.q: Bilateral sacroiliitis on imaging in early axial disease is described in the source as what?
opts: An exclusive feature of psoriatic arthritis
questions.exp: Under synovitis, B/L sacroiliitis is annotated as hallmark and earliest manifestation. (Book p533)

questions.sec: Radiographic axial SpA pathogenesis, presentation and inflammatory back pain
questions.q: What sex ratio, age group and HLA frequency are printed for ankylosing spondylitis presentation?
opts: M:F 3:1, early 20s, HLA B27 in 90% of AS
Equal sex ratio, children under 10, B27 negative
questions.exp: Presentation prints M:F = 3:1, age early 20s and HLA B27 association in 90% of AS. (Book p533)

questions.sec: Radiographic axial SpA pathogenesis, presentation and inflammatory back pain
questions.q: Among enthesitis sites, which is called classical in the source?
questions.exp: Enthesitis examples: Achilles tendinitis is annotated classical; plantar fasciitis and costochondritis follow. (Book p533)

questions.sec: Radiographic axial SpA pathogenesis, presentation and inflammatory back pain
questions.q: A patient reports morning back stiffness lasting about 45 minutes that improves with exercise and NSAIDs but not with rest. Which printed aspects are satisfied?
opts: Onset after age 60 with rapid response to bed rest
Shorter than 2 weeks with worsening on activity
Location confined to the neck with no buttock pain
Duration over 3 months, improvement with exercise, improvement with NSAIDs and no improvement with rest
questions.exp: Inflammatory back pain aspects: duration >3 months (chronic), improvement with exercise, improvement with NSAIDs and no improvement of pain with rest; morning stiffness minimum 30 minutes. (Book p533)

questions.sec: Radiographic axial SpA pathogenesis, presentation and inflammatory back pain
questions.q: Which onset and location details are printed for inflammatory back pain?
opts: Onset before 45 years with lower-back location and alternating buttock pain
Onset after 70 years confined to the thoracic spine
Onset in childhood with isolated cervical pain
No defined age with constant midline pain only
questions.exp: Aspects list onset before 45 yrs, location lower back and alternating buttock pain. (Book p533)

questions.sec: Radiographic axial SpA pathogenesis, presentation and inflammatory back pain
questions.q: What minimum morning stiffness duration and waking-from-sleep feature are printed?
opts: Morning stiffness of at least 30 minutes with waking from sleep due to back pain
Stiffness under 10 minutes without nocturnal waking
questions.exp: Aspects include waking up from sleep due to back pain and morning stiffness (minimum 30 mins). (Book p533)

questions.sec: Radiographic axial SpA pathogenesis, presentation and inflammatory back pain
questions.q: Involvement of shoulders and hip joints in axial SpA is annotated in the source as indicating what?
questions.exp: The final inflammatory-back-pain aspect annotates involvement of shoulders and hip joint as poor prognosis. (Book p533)

questions.sec: Radiographic axial SpA pathogenesis, presentation and inflammatory back pain
questions.q: Which extra-articular list belongs to radiographic axial SpA on this page?
opts: Only palmar plantar pustulosis without eye disease
Membranous nephropathy with Hearing loss only
4A uveitis (m/c), aortic regurgitation/ascending aortitis/conduction blocks, secondary IgA nephropathy, upper-lobe NSIP, enthesitis-related chest pain and osteoporosis
questions.exp: Extra-articular features print 4A uveitis m/c; CVS aortic regurgitation, ascending aortitis, conduction blocks; renal secondary IgA nephropathy; lungs upper lobe interstitial lung disease (NSIP); chest pain from costochondritis/manubriosternal enthesitis plus ascending thoracic spine; and osteoporosis. (Book p533)

questions.sec: Radiographic axial SpA pathogenesis, presentation and inflammatory back pain
questions.q: Chest pain in a patient with ankylosing spondylitis is attributed in the text to which mechanism?
opts: Enthesitis at costochondritis or manubriosternal joint plus ascending thoracic spine involvement
questions.exp: Chest pain is d/t enthesitis at costochondritis or manubriosternal joint plus ascending thoracic spine. (Book p533)

questions.sec: Investigation: MRI-STIR, sacroiliitis x-ray grading and radiographic signs
questions.q: Which conditions are paired with upper-lobe interstitial lung disease in the printed note?
questions.exp: Note: Upper Lobe ILD — sarcoidosis, ankylosing spondylitis. (Book p534)

questions.sec: Investigation: MRI-STIR, sacroiliitis x-ray grading and radiographic signs
questions.q: What osteoporosis frequency ranking is printed?
questions.exp: Note prints osteoporosis: RA > AS > sarcoidosis > SLE. (Book p534)

questions.sec: Investigation: MRI-STIR, sacroiliitis x-ray grading and radiographic signs
questions.q: What does STIR stand for in the printed investigation note, and how is hyperintensity interpreted?
opts: Signal Transfer Inversion Recovery; hyperintensity is diagnostic
Saturation Through Inversion Recovery; hyperintensity excludes disease
Short Time Inversion Region; hyperintensity is pathognomonic
Short Tau Inversion Recovery; hyperintensity is inconclusive
questions.exp: Investigation: MRI — STIR sequence; STIR = Short Tau Inversion Recovery; hyperintensity: inconclusive. (Book p534)

questions.sec: Investigation: MRI-STIR, sacroiliitis x-ray grading and radiographic signs
questions.q: Which MRI panel labels are printed beneath the sacroiliac images?
opts: Semi-coronal T1, semi-coronal T1FS, semi-coronal STIR and semi-axial STIR
Only AP pelvis and lateral views
questions.exp: The MRI strip is captioned semi-coronal T1, semi-coronal T1FS, semi-coronal STIR and semi-axial STIR. (Book p534)

questions.sec: Investigation: MRI-STIR, sacroiliitis x-ray grading and radiographic signs
questions.q: What is printed as grade 0 of sacroiliitis on plain x-ray?
questions.exp: Grade 0 caption reads normal joints. (Book p534)

questions.sec: Investigation: MRI-STIR, sacroiliitis x-ray grading and radiographic signs
questions.q: Which grade description and timing label apply to the earliest x-ray sign of sacroiliitis?
opts: Grade 3: loss of margins and widening of joint space
Grade 1: slight blurring of cortical margins of the lower one-third of each joint; earliest x-ray sign
questions.exp: Grade 1 shows slight blurring of cortical margins of lower 1/3rd of each joint and is marked earliest x-ray sign. (Book p534)

questions.sec: Investigation: MRI-STIR, sacroiliitis x-ray grading and radiographic signs
questions.q: What two findings define grade 2 of sacroiliitis in the source?
opts: Loss of margins and joint-space widening
questions.exp: Grade 2 caption: blurring + sclerosis. (Book p534)

questions.sec: Investigation: MRI-STIR, sacroiliitis x-ray grading and radiographic signs
questions.q: What two findings define grade 3 of sacroiliitis?
opts: Loss of margins and widening of joint space
questions.exp: Grade 3 lists loss of margins and widening of joint space. (Book p534)

questions.sec: Investigation: MRI-STIR, sacroiliitis x-ray grading and radiographic signs
questions.q: What single finding defines grade 4 of sacroiliitis?
questions.exp: Grade 4 caption: joint ankylosis. (Book p534)

questions.sec: Investigation: MRI-STIR, sacroiliitis x-ray grading and radiographic signs
questions.q: Bilateral sacroiliitis reported as grade 2/3 with a separate bamboo-spine film matches which printed pair of captions?
opts: Unilateral grade 1 only and square vertebra
questions.exp: The page captions B/L sacroiliitis (grade 2/3) and a bamboo spine image. (Book p534)

questions.sec: Investigation: MRI-STIR, sacroiliitis x-ray grading and radiographic signs
questions.q: Which structure calcification produces the dagger sign on AP spine films?
questions.exp: Dagger sign: calcification of interspinous ligament; shown with dagger spine, rail-road sign and trolley-track sign panels. (Book p535)

questions.sec: Investigation: MRI-STIR, sacroiliitis x-ray grading and radiographic signs
questions.q: Which structure calcification produces the trolley track sign?
questions.exp: Trolley track sign: calcification of joint capsule. (Book p535)

questions.sec: Investigation: MRI-STIR, sacroiliitis x-ray grading and radiographic signs
questions.q: What is the Romanus sign and its printed downstream signs?
opts: Erosion of the vertebral corner, then shiny-corner sclerosis, then square-wave vertebra with loss of concavity
questions.exp: Romanus sign: erosion of corner; shiny corner sign: sclerosis of vertebra; square wave vertebra: vertebra become square-like. (Book p535)

questions.sec: Investigation: MRI-STIR, sacroiliitis x-ray grading and radiographic signs
questions.q: In the modified Schober test, what are the landmark and the A-to-B distance marked on the diagram?
opts: ASIS with A to B = 20 cm
Sacrococcygeal junction with A to B = 25 cm
Posterior superior iliac spine landmark with A to B = 15 cm (10 cm above plus 5 cm below)
Iliac crest with A to B = 5 cm
questions.exp: Landmark is posterior superior iliac spine; diagram labels A to B = 15 cm with 10 cm and 5 cm segments. (Book p535)

questions.sec: Investigation: MRI-STIR, sacroiliitis x-ray grading and radiographic signs
questions.q: During modified Schober testing the patient bends forward with knees extended and the A-to-B span measures 17 cm. How is this classified?
opts: Normal, because the minimum is 15 cm
Normal only if the knees are flexed
Abnormal, because A to B under 20 cm is abnormal
questions.exp: Forward bending with knee in extension; A to B 20 cm (minimum) is normal, less than 20 cm is abnormal. (Book p535)

questions.sec: Investigation: MRI-STIR, sacroiliitis x-ray grading and radiographic signs
questions.q: How are non-radiographic axial SpA and ankylosing spondylitis managed first in the printed algorithm?
opts: Non-radiographic axial SpA: NSAIDs when needed; AS: exercise and physiotherapy as most important
Bed rest for both until symptoms resolve
Opioids as first line for both
questions.exp: Treatment: non-radiological axial SpA — NSAIDs when needed; AS — exercise, physiotherapy (most important). (Book p535)

questions.sec: Investigation: MRI-STIR, sacroiliitis x-ray grading and radiographic signs
questions.q: Which first-line NSAID regimen and duration purpose are printed for AS?
opts: Methotrexate 15 mg weekly as first line
Indomethacin 50 mg TID (also naproxen, ibuprofen); first line that prevents progression; duration 2–3 weeks
questions.exp: NSAID: indomethacin 50 mg TID, naproxen, ibuprofen — first line, prevent progression of disease, duration 2–3 wks. (Book p535)

questions.sec: Advanced therapy, DISH and reactive arthritis onset
questions.q: Which biologic pair is printed after the NSAID block for axial SpA?
opts: Abatacept and anakinra as the only options
questions.exp: The treatment continuation prints anti TNF alpha: adalimumab and anti IL-17: secukinumab. (Book p536)

questions.sec: Advanced therapy, DISH and reactive arthritis onset
questions.q: What is the printed role of intra-articular steroids in this chapter?
questions.exp: Intra-articular steroids: for pain relief. (Book p536)

questions.sec: Advanced therapy, DISH and reactive arthritis onset
questions.q: What demographic and inflammatory profile is printed for DISH?
opts: Elderly male, non-inflammatory, part of metabolic syndrome
Young female with raised ESR as the rule
Acute inflammatory monoarthritis of the first MTP
questions.exp: DISH (diffuse idiopathic skeletal hyperostosis): elderly male, non-inflammatory, part of metabolic syndrome. (Book p536)

questions.sec: Advanced therapy, DISH and reactive arthritis onset
questions.q: Which structural and radiographic features complete the printed DISH description?
opts: Ligamentous calcification with flowing wax appearance on x-ray
Marginal syndesmophytes with bamboo spine only
questions.exp: DISH lists ligamentous calcification and flowing wax appearance in x-ray; dorsal and lumbar spine films illustrate the flow. (Book p536)

questions.sec: Advanced therapy, DISH and reactive arthritis onset
questions.q: What former name and classic triad are printed for reactive arthritis?
opts: Behcet triad of oral and genital ulcers with uveitis only
Reiter as a seronegative RA subtype
Whipple disease triad of malabsorption and arthralgia
questions.exp: Reactive arthritis was previously known as Reiter's syndrome (urethritis, arthritis, conjunctivitis). (Book p536)

questions.sec: Advanced therapy, DISH and reactive arthritis onset
questions.q: Which extra-articular feature and demographic pattern are printed for reactive arthritis?
opts: Chronic posterior uveitis with female predominance over 60
No ocular involvement with equal sex ratio in children
4A uveitis as most common; male greater than female, age 20–40 years
questions.exp: m/c extra-articular manifestation: 4A uveitis; m > F, 20–40 yrs. (Book p536)

questions.sec: Advanced therapy, DISH and reactive arthritis onset
questions.q: What interval and axial involvement percentage appear on the infection-to-arthritis flowchart?
opts: Infection after 2–4 weeks leads to arthritis, with axial involvement in 30%
Infection same day with axial involvement in 5%
Infection after 6 months with axial involvement in 80%
No latency with axial involvement in 10%
questions.exp: Flowchart: infection → 2–4 weeks → arthritis with peripheral and axial (30%) arms. (Book p536)

questions.sec: Advanced therapy, DISH and reactive arthritis onset
questions.q: What percentage of reactive arthritis episodes is printed as progressing to chronic arthritis?
questions.exp: The flowchart prints 20% progressing to chronic arthritis. (Book p536)

questions.sec: Advanced therapy, DISH and reactive arthritis onset
questions.q: Which genitourinary trigger and sex ratio are printed as most common worldwide?
questions.exp: Genitourinary: Chlamydia trachomatis (m/c cause worldwide) with M:F = 9:1. (Book p536)

questions.sec: Advanced therapy, DISH and reactive arthritis onset
questions.q: Which gastrointestinal trigger is most common in India, and what is its sex ratio?
questions.exp: Gastrointestinal: Shigella flexneri (m/c cause in India) with M:F = 1:1; Salmonella and Campylobacter follow. (Book p536)

questions.sec: Advanced therapy, DISH and reactive arthritis onset
questions.q: Which organisms are explicitly excluded as causative agents of reactive arthritis on this page?
questions.exp: Note: E. coli and neisseria are not causative agents. (Book p536)

questions.sec: Reactive arthritis clinical course, mucocutaneous lesions and axial involvement
questions.q: Synovial fluid cultures are sterile but PCR detects organism DNA inside synovial monocytes. Which printed concept applies?
opts: Acute sterile arthritis with organisms inside synovial monocytes detected by PCR
questions.exp: Acute sterile arthritis: organism not isolated from synovial fluid; organisms inside monocytes of synovium are detected by PCR of synovial fluid. (Book p537)

questions.sec: Reactive arthritis clinical course, mucocutaneous lesions and axial involvement
questions.q: What HLA B27 percentage in reactive arthritis is linked to chronicity and prognosis?
questions.exp: HLA B-27 association in 50%–70% cases is linked to chronicity and prognosis. (Book p537)

questions.sec: Reactive arthritis clinical course, mucocutaneous lesions and axial involvement
questions.q: A patient's arthritis starts in one knee and later adds joints asymmetrically with pain. Which printed pattern is this?
opts: Symmetrical small-joint polyarthritis of MCP joints only
Isolated axial disease without peripheral joints
Asymmetrical peripheral arthritis starting at the knee with oligoarthritis greater than monoarthritis, additive and painful
questions.exp: Asymmetrical peripheral arthritis: starts at knee joint; oligoarthritis greater than monoarthritis; additive — progressive involvement of joints; painful. (Book p537)

questions.sec: Reactive arthritis clinical course, mucocutaneous lesions and axial involvement
questions.q: Which clinical manifestation triad is printed for reactive arthritis?
opts: Synovitis plus predominant enthesitis plus dactylitis
Fever plus rash plus lymphadenopathy alone
questions.exp: Clinical manifestations: synovitis plus predominant enthesitis plus dactylitis; images show Achilles enthesitis and sausage-digit dactylitis. (Book p537)

questions.sec: Reactive arthritis clinical course, mucocutaneous lesions and axial involvement
questions.q: How are keratoderma blennorrhagicum and circinate balanitis described?
opts: Keratoderma: hyperkeratotic crusty painless vesicles on palms and soles; balanitis: shallow painless erythematous glans ulcers
Both are painful ulcerative lesions only on soles
Keratoderma is pustular only on the trunk
questions.exp: 1. Keratoderma blennorrhagicum: hyperkeratotic, crusty vesicles on palms and soles, painless. 2. Circinate balanitis: shallow erythematous ulcers of glans penis, painless. (Book p537)

questions.sec: Reactive arthritis clinical course, mucocutaneous lesions and axial involvement
questions.q: What is the printed differential diagnosis of keratoderma blennorrhagicum?
questions.exp: Note: D/d for keratoderma blennorrhagicum — palmo-plantar psoriasis. (Book p537)

questions.sec: Reactive arthritis clinical course, mucocutaneous lesions and axial involvement
questions.q: What percentage develops axial involvement in reactive arthritis, and what pattern of sacroiliitis is printed?
questions.exp: Axial involvement of reactive arthritis (30%) with asymmetric sacroiliitis. (Book p537)

questions.sec: Reactive arthritis clinical course, mucocutaneous lesions and axial involvement
questions.q: Which syndesmophyte morphology is printed for reactive arthritis axial disease?
opts: Thick, large, coarse, fluffy and non-marginal due to paravertebral ossification
questions.exp: Syndesmophytes d/t paravertebral ossification: thick, large, coarse, fluffy, non-marginal. (Book p537)

questions.sec: Reactive arthritis systemic features, treatment and enteropathic arthritis
questions.q: Which cardiac and renal extra-articular features are printed for reactive arthritis?
opts: Aortic regurgitation (most common) with conduction blocks; secondary IgA nephropathy
questions.exp: Other manifestations: heart — aortic regurgitation (m/c), conduction blocks; kidney — secondary IgA nephropathy. (Book p538)

questions.sec: Reactive arthritis systemic features, treatment and enteropathic arthritis
questions.q: What outcome statement is printed for reactive arthritis chronicity?
opts: Chronic arthritis occurs only after eye involvement
Outcome/chronicity is unrelated to initial severity
Only severe index episodes become chronic
questions.exp: Outcome/chronicity: unrelated to initial severity. (Book p538)

questions.sec: Reactive arthritis systemic features, treatment and enteropathic arthritis
questions.q: Which laboratory and microbiology investigations are printed?
opts: Low ESR with negative PCR as the rule
Serum RF as the diagnostic test
Raised ESR/CRP and synovial-fluid PCR that identifies the organism
questions.exp: Investigations: ESR CRP increased; synovial fluid PCR identifies organism. (Book p538)

questions.sec: Reactive arthritis systemic features, treatment and enteropathic arthritis
questions.q: Migratory upper- and lower-limb arthritis is highlighted in the source against which organism?
questions.exp: Note: gonococcal arthritis has migratory upper limb and lower limb arthritis. (Book p538)

questions.sec: Reactive arthritis systemic features, treatment and enteropathic arthritis
questions.q: Which reactive arthritis treatment triplet is printed?
opts: Indomethacin 50 mg TID, intra-articular steroid for pain, and sulfasalazine for chronic disease (15%–20%)
Methotrexate as first line without NSAIDs
questions.exp: Treatment: NSAIDs — indomethacin 50 mg TID; intraarticular steroid to alleviate pain; DMARD — sulfasalazine for chronic reactive arthritis (15%–20%). (Book p538)

questions.sec: Reactive arthritis systemic features, treatment and enteropathic arthritis
questions.q: What alternate name, sex ratio and IBD hierarchy are printed for enteropathic arthritis?
opts: Psoriatic variant with no bowel link
IBD-associated arthritis; M:F 1:1; Crohn disease greater than ulcerative colitis
Seronegative spondyloarthritis with male predominance; UC greater than Crohn
questions.exp: Enteropathic arthritis AKA IBD associated arthritis; M:F = 1:1; Crohn's disease greater than ulcerative colitis. (Book p538)

questions.sec: Reactive arthritis systemic features, treatment and enteropathic arthritis
questions.q: Which peripheral versus axial pattern percentages are printed for enteropathic arthritis?
questions.exp: Peripheral (25%) greater than axial pattern (10%). (Book p538)

questions.sec: Reactive arthritis systemic features, treatment and enteropathic arthritis
questions.q: Which features define axial enteropathic arthritis on this page?
opts: Presentation similar to ankylosing spondylitis with HLA B27 in 50%, symmetric sacroiliitis, no correlation to bowel activity, no enthesitis or dactylitis
Asymmetric sacroiliitis with dactylitis as the rule
questions.exp: Axial arthritis: presentation similar to ankylosing spondylitis; HLA B-27 association in 50% cases; symmetric sacroiliitis; no correlation to bowel activity; no enthesitis, dactylitis. (Book p538)

questions.sec: Reactive arthritis systemic features, treatment and enteropathic arthritis
questions.q: In the peripheral arthritis table, which associations belong to Type 1 LMAP arthritis?
opts: Episcleritis, erythema nodosum and arthritis, with flares correlating with bowel disease and more common occurrence
Uveitis with no correlation and less common occurrence
questions.exp: Type 1 LMAP arthritis: more common; flares correlate with bowel disease; associated factors episcleritis, erythema nodosum, arthritis — versus Type 2 SMAP-u: less common, no correlation, uveitis. (Book p538)

questions.sec: LMAP versus SMAP-u, stool markers and psoriatic arthritis basics
questions.q: Which pattern description belongs to Type 1 LMAP arthritis?
opts: Strictly axial with no peripheral joints
Large joint (knee predominant), migratory, asymmetric, pauciarticular with lower limb greater than upper limb
Small joint MCP, aggressive chronic symmetric polyarticular
questions.exp: Type 1 LMAP arthritis row: large joint (knee predominant), migratory, asymmetric, pauciarticular arthritis (lower limb greater than upper limb). (Book p539)

questions.sec: LMAP versus SMAP-u, stool markers and psoriatic arthritis basics
questions.q: Which treatment and prognosis pair is printed for Type 1 LMAP arthritis?
opts: Anti-TNF alpha (infliximab) as drug of choice
questions.exp: Type 1 treatment/prognosis: self-limiting, good prognosis. (Book p539)

questions.sec: LMAP versus SMAP-u, stool markers and psoriatic arthritis basics
questions.q: Which pattern belongs to Type 2 SMAP-u arthritis?
opts: Small joint (MCP), migratory, aggressive chronic, symmetrical polyarticular arthritis
questions.exp: Type 2 SMAP-u arthritis: small joint (MCP), migratory, aggressive, chronic, symmetrical, polyarticular arthritis. (Book p539)

questions.sec: LMAP versus SMAP-u, stool markers and psoriatic arthritis basics
questions.q: What is the printed drug of choice for Type 2 SMAP-u arthritis?
questions.exp: Type 2 treatment: anti TNF alpha — DOC, infliximab. (Book p539)

questions.sec: LMAP versus SMAP-u, stool markers and psoriatic arthritis basics
questions.q: Which stool markers are printed for monitoring bowel flares?
opts: Occult blood alone as the sole marker
questions.exp: Note: calprotectin, lactoferrin in stools for bowel flare. (Book p539)

questions.sec: LMAP versus SMAP-u, stool markers and psoriatic arthritis basics
questions.q: What proportion of psoriatic cases develops arthritis, and which psoriasis type is linked?
questions.exp: Psoriatic arthritis: 7%–40% of psoriatic cases develop arthritis; plaque type psoriasis. (Book p539)

questions.sec: LMAP versus SMAP-u, stool markers and psoriatic arthritis basics
questions.q: What age, sex ratio and HLA associations are printed for psoriatic arthritis?
opts: Age over 40, M:F 1:1, HLA CW-06 02 and HLA B27 for arthritis
Age under 20 with HLA DR4 only
questions.exp: Age greater than 40 yrs; M:F = 1:1; HLA CW-06 02, HLA B27 (arthritis). (Book p539)

questions.sec: LMAP versus SMAP-u, stool markers and psoriatic arthritis basics
questions.q: How does the 60/30/30 rule distribute psoriasis–arthritis order, and what nail percentage is bracketed?
opts: 60% psoriasis then arthritis; 20% both together; 20% arthritis then psoriasis; nail changes in 90%
questions.exp: 60/30/30 rule: 60% psoriasis → arthritis, 20% psoriasis + arthritis, 20% arthritis → psoriasis, plus nail changes in 90%. (Book p539)

questions.sec: LMAP versus SMAP-u, stool markers and psoriatic arthritis basics
questions.q: Which clinical manifestation cluster is printed for psoriatic arthritis?
opts: Synovitis, dactylitis, enthesitis and axial involvement of the cervical spine
questions.exp: Clinical manifestation: synovitis + dactylitis + enthesitis + axial involvement (cervical spine). (Book p539)

questions.sec: LMAP versus SMAP-u, stool markers and psoriatic arthritis basics
questions.q: Which joint morphology and mucocutaneous statement are printed?
opts: Thin marginal symmetrical syndesmophytes with obligatory rash
Punched-out erosions with pathognomonic nail loss only
Pure cartilage loss without bone change
Thick, non-marginal, asymmetric arthritis with no mucocutaneous involvement at the articular assessment
questions.exp: Thick, non-marginal, asymmetric arthritis; no mucocutaneous involvement is listed in the manifestation block. (Book p539)

questions.sec: LMAP versus SMAP-u, stool markers and psoriatic arthritis basics
questions.q: Which cardiac, renal and ocular extras complete the psoriatic arthritis list?
opts: Aortic regurgitation with conduction block; secondary IgA nephropathy; bilateral chronic posterior uveitis
Mitral prolapse with interstitial nephritis and anterior uveitis
questions.exp: CVS: aortic regurgitation, conduction block; renal: 2° IgA nephropathy; B/L chronic posterior uveitis. (Book p539)

questions.sec: Psoriasis variants, nail signs and Wright–Moll classification
questions.q: Which psoriasis forms are annotated as not associated with arthritis?
questions.exp: The captions guttate psoriasis and erythrodermis psoriasis carry the note not associated with arthritis. (Book p540)

questions.sec: Psoriasis variants, nail signs and Wright–Moll classification
questions.q: Pustular psoriasis with destructive joint disease prompts which printed instruction?
opts: Rule out HIV; it is the most destructive arthritis pattern
questions.exp: Pustular psoriasis: most destructive arthritis; rule out HIV. (Book p540)

questions.sec: Psoriasis variants, nail signs and Wright–Moll classification
questions.q: What percentage of psoriatic patients has nail changes, and what yellow-margin pattern is printed?
opts: 100% with complete nail loss at onset
questions.exp: Nail changes (90%): yellow nail margin (longitudinal). (Book p540)

questions.sec: Psoriasis variants, nail signs and Wright–Moll classification
questions.q: Which four nail photographs are labeled on this page?
opts: Deep and coarse nail pitting; onycholysis with subungual hyperkeratosis; oil drop sign (classical); longitudinal ridging
questions.exp: Nail panels: deep and coarse nail pitting; onycholysis with subungual hyperkeratosis; oil drop sign (classical); longitudinal ridging. (Book p540)

questions.sec: Psoriasis variants, nail signs and Wright–Moll classification
questions.q: Which nail sign is explicitly called classical?
questions.exp: The oil drop sign panel is annotated classical. (Book p540)

questions.sec: Psoriasis variants, nail signs and Wright–Moll classification
questions.q: Which pattern is the most common type in the Wright and Moll classification?
opts: Symmetric polyarthritis with DIP involvement, skin lesions and nail changes, differentially RA in small joints
questions.exp: Wright and Moll: symmetric polyarthritis (m/c type) — involvement of DIP, skin lesion, nail changes; D/d RA (involvement of small joints). (Book p540)

questions.sec: Psoriasis variants, nail signs and Wright–Moll classification
questions.q: Which remaining Wright–Moll patterns are printed?
opts: Asymmetrical oligoarthritis; predominant DIP arthritis; predominant spondyloarthritis (axial 5%, cervical predominance); arthritis mutilans with complete destruction
questions.exp: Classification continues with asymmetrical oligoarthritis, predominant DIP arthritis, predominant spondyloarthritis (axial pattern 5%, cervical predominance) and arthritis mutilans: complete destruction. (Book p540)

questions.sec: Psoriasis variants, nail signs and Wright–Moll classification
questions.q: What axial percentage and region predominance are printed for the spondyloarthritis pattern of psoriatic arthritis?
questions.exp: Predominant spondyloarthritis: axial pattern (5%), cervical predominance. (Book p540)

questions.sec: Psoriatic versus rheumatoid features, progression and hand radiographs
questions.q: Which three clinical images are captioned on this page?
opts: Arthritis mutilans, dactylitis and corn foot
Gouty tophi, chalky deposit and bursitis
Heberden nodes, Bouchard nodes and swan neck
questions.exp: Image captions: arthritis mutilans; dactylitis; corn foot. (Book p541)

questions.sec: Psoriatic versus rheumatoid features, progression and hand radiographs
questions.q: In the PsA versus RA table, how is psoriasis scored in each column?
opts: Psoriatic arthritis plus; rheumatoid arthritis minus
questions.exp: Difference table row Psoriasis: psoriatic arthritis +, rheumatoid arthritis −. (Book p541)

questions.sec: Psoriatic versus rheumatoid features, progression and hand radiographs
questions.q: Which row favors rheumatoid arthritis rather than psoriatic arthritis in the printed table?
opts: Nail dystrophy present only in PsA
Symmetric disease scored ++ in RA versus + in PsA
questions.exp: Symmetric: RA ++ greater than PsA +, while asymmetric, enthesopathy, dactylitis, nail dystrophy and HIV association favor PsA. (Book p541)

questions.sec: Psoriatic versus rheumatoid features, progression and hand radiographs
questions.q: Which features are printed as present in psoriatic arthritis but absent in rheumatoid arthritis?
opts: Enthesopathy, dactylitis, nail dystrophy and HIV association
questions.exp: Table rows enthesopathy, dactylitis, nail dystrophy and HIV association are + for PsA and − for RA. (Book p541)

questions.sec: Psoriatic versus rheumatoid features, progression and hand radiographs
questions.q: What progression statement and classification criteria are printed for psoriatic arthritis?
opts: Rapid progression to bony ankylosis with CASPER criteria and no diagnostic testing
Slow progression with ACR 1987 as the only criteria
No bony change with mandatory serology
questions.exp: Progression: rapid progression to bony ankylosis; CASPER criteria; no diagnostic testing. (Book p541)

questions.sec: Psoriatic versus rheumatoid features, progression and hand radiographs
questions.q: What does the ivory phalanx radiograph represent in this chapter?
opts: A septic arthritis with osteomyelitis only
A psoriatic hand finding shown beside the progression notes
A gouty tophus with rat-bite erosions
questions.exp: The page pairs an ivory phalanx hand film with the progression and CASPER notes for psoriatic arthritis. (Book p541)

questions.sec: Psoriatic versus rheumatoid features, progression and hand radiographs
questions.q: How are syndesmophytes defined in the AP vertebral diagram on this page?
questions.exp: Syndesmophytes: thin, vertical and symmetrical in the AP illustration. (Book p541)

questions.sec: Psoriatic spinal and hand radiographic signs plus systemic therapy
questions.q: How is paravertebral ossification characterized and which diseases are listed?
opts: Large, coarse and asymmetrical; seen in Reiter's syndrome and psoriatic arthropathy
Thin and marginal only in ankylosing spondylitis
questions.exp: Paravertebral ossification: large, coarse, asymmetrical; seen in Reiter's syndrome and psoriatic arthropathy; the film is captioned non-marginal syndesmophyte. (Book p542)

questions.sec: Psoriatic spinal and hand radiographic signs plus systemic therapy
questions.q: What is the pencil-in-cup deformity shown on the hand film and diagram?
opts: Tapered proximal phalanx fitting a widened distal articular cup
questions.exp: Pencil-in-cup deformity is illustrated radiographically and schematically versus a normal phalanx. (Book p542)

questions.sec: Psoriatic spinal and hand radiographic signs plus systemic therapy
questions.q: How is whiskering defined in the source?
opts: Punched-out lesion with sclerotic rim only
Marginal erosion with adjacent bone proliferation
Sclerosis of the vertebral corner only
questions.exp: Whiskering: marginal erosion with adjacent bone proliferation. (Book p542)

questions.sec: Psoriatic spinal and hand radiographic signs plus systemic therapy
questions.q: What two additional hand signs are listed with whiskering?
opts: Heberden nodes and swan-neck deformity only
Nail pitting alone without bone change
Telescoping of digits and ray pattern erosion of MCP, PIP and DIP in the same finger (100% psoriatic x-ray)
questions.exp: Telescoping of digits; ray pattern — erosion of MCP, PIP, DIP in same finger; 100% psoriatic X-ray. (Book p542)

questions.sec: Psoriatic spinal and hand radiographic signs plus systemic therapy
questions.q: Which full medication list is printed for psoriatic arthritis?
opts: Anti-TNF alpha drugs, apremilast (PDE4 inhibitor), methotrexate, leflunomide, ustekinumab, secukinumab and tofacitinib
questions.exp: Treatment lists anti TNF alpha drugs, apremilast (PDE 4 inhibitor), methotrexate, leflunomide, ustekinumab, secukinumab and tofacitinib. (Book p542)

questions.sec: Psoriatic spinal and hand radiographic signs plus systemic therapy
questions.q: Which mechanism label is attached to apremilast in the printed ladder?
questions.exp: Apremilast is annotated PDE 4 inhibitor. (Book p542)

units.title: 1. Spondyloarthritis classification, shared features and non-radiographic axial SpA
units.sec: Spondyloarthritis classification, shared features and non-radiographic axial SpA
units.guide:
The chapter opens with the axial, peripheral and juvenile SpA tree and shared features. Non-radiographic axial SpA clinical features, MRI note and 5% progression in 5–10 years are kept in printed order.
Radiographic conversion brings sacroiliitis x-ray features and extra-articular may be seen.

units.title: 2. Radiographic axial SpA pathogenesis, presentation and inflammatory back pain
units.sec: Radiographic axial SpA pathogenesis, presentation and inflammatory back pain
units.guide:
Inflammatory granulation tissue erodes disc structures and calcifies annular fibres into syndesmophytes. Vertical osteophytes, gliding, bony ankylosis, bamboo spine and square-wave vertebra complete the mechanical chain.
Complication, mediators, synovitis–enthesitis presentation and inflammatory back pain aspects follow source order.

units.title: 3. Investigation: MRI-STIR, sacroiliitis x-ray grading and radiographic signs
units.sec: Investigation: MRI-STIR, sacroiliitis x-ray grading and radiographic signs
units.guide:
Upper-lobe ILD and osteoporosis ranking notes precede the MRI-STIR block. Plain x-ray grades 0–4 of sacroiliitis with the earliest sign and bamboo spine close the imaging unit.
Dagger, trolley-track, Romanus, shiny-corner and square-wave signs are kept as printed definitions.

units.title: 4. Advanced therapy, DISH and reactive arthritis onset
units.sec: Advanced therapy, DISH and reactive arthritis onset
units.guide:
Adalimumab, secukinumab and intra-articular steroids complete axial therapy. DISH demographics, metabolic link and flowing-wax x-ray appearance open the differential block.
Reiter's triad, 4A uveitis, demographics, infection-to-arthritis timing and trigger organisms stay in printed order.

units.title: 5. Reactive arthritis clinical course, mucocutaneous lesions and axial involvement
units.sec: Reactive arthritis clinical course, mucocutaneous lesions and axial involvement
units.guide:
Sterile arthritis, PCR detection and HLA-B27 chronicity precede the asymmetrical pattern. Synovitis–enthesitis–dactylitis, keratoderma and circinate balanitis with psoriasis d/d follow.
Axial 30% with fluffy non-marginal syndesmophytes closes the block.

units.title: 6. Reactive arthritis systemic features, treatment and enteropathic arthritis
units.sec: Reactive arthritis systemic features, treatment and enteropathic arthritis
units.guide:
Cardiac and renal extras plus severity-independent outcome lead investigations. Gonococcal migratory note and the indomethacin–sulfasalazine ladder complete reactive therapy.
Enteropathic epidemiology, axial features and the LMAP versus SMAP-u table follow in printed order.

units.title: 7. LMAP versus SMAP-u, stool markers and psoriatic arthritis basics
units.sec: LMAP versus SMAP-u, stool markers and psoriatic arthritis basics
units.guide:
The arthritis-pattern table contrasts large-joint self-limited disease with aggressive small-joint polyarthritis needing anti-TNF. Stool calprotectin/lactoferrin note transitions to psoriatic arthritis epidemiology and HLA links.
The 60/30/30 rule with 90% nail changes and systemic manifestations stay source-ordered.

units.title: 8. Psoriasis variants, nail signs and Wright–Moll classification
units.sec: Psoriasis variants, nail signs and Wright–Moll classification
units.guide:
Guttate/erythrodermic forms are separated from arthritis while pustular disease is most destructive. Five nail photographs with oil-drop sign as classical map the 90% nail-change rule.
Wright–Moll five patterns including arthritis mutilans close the unit in printed order.

units.title: 9. Psoriatic versus rheumatoid features, progression and hand radiographs
units.sec: Psoriatic versus rheumatoid features, progression and hand radiographs
units.guide:
Mutilans, dactylitis and corn-foot images open the unit. The eight-row PsA-versus-RA comparison table and rapid bony ankylosis with CASPER follow.
Ivory phalanx and thin vertical symmetrical syndesmophytes close the page.

units.title: 10. Psoriatic spinal and hand radiographic signs plus systemic therapy
units.sec: Psoriatic spinal and hand radiographic signs plus systemic therapy
units.guide:
Paravertebral ossification and non-marginal syndesmophytes contrast with axial AS morphology. Pencil-in-cup, whiskering, telescoping and the 100% ray pattern define PsA hands.
The seven-drug ladder from anti-TNF to tofacitinib closes Chapter 27 in printed order.
